reply_text:
Now the race case itself, simulated: the loop changes one row while someone else adds a row to the file on disk.The rebase keeps both writers' rows. Next, the loop's handling of failed jobs:Testing the new branch with the two real failed jobs from last night, plus a failure after execution with no receipt:All three cases behave as intended. Committing and restarting both loops:I stopped both loops, fixed two problems, and restarted them at 01:22. topo1 is back on t98A06 and topo2 has picked its job back up (ab9f8db7).

**What caused the repairs.** There were three supervisor repairs: topo1 at 23:54, and topo2 at 00:01 and 00:10. All three came from futon1b being overloaded, which you've since fixed. Its request queue was waiting 120–145 s, so the Agency couldn't read or write its per-turn records in time. Two things made the loops handle that badly:
- **Two failed before the seat did anything** (`store-busy`). The loop only knew to retry specific error codes, so it treated these as fatal. The 23:56 fix covered only this one code.
- **One failed after the seat had finished** (`activity-decision-failed` at 00:10). The seat had done its work and written its receipt. Only the Agency's record-keeping afterwards failed, so a completed job was thrown away and a repair was spent.

**Fix 1: failed jobs.** When a job fails, the loop now checks two things before calling a repair:
- If the seat's last message contains its receipt, the loop uses it as a completed job. The usual receipt checks still apply.
- If the seat never ran anything, the loop waits and resends, whatever the error code.

A failure after real work with no receipt still goes to repair, as before. I tested this on the two real failed jobs from last night and on a made-up failure of the third kind. All three behaved as intended.

**Fix 2: worklist writes, the race that dropped my t99J04 row.**
- The loop now re-reads the worklist just before writing, and applies only its own row changes to what's on disk.
- It checks the file again after validation, which takes a few seconds, and redoes the merge if the file changed meanwhile.

A simulated race test kept both the hand-added row and the loop's own edit. All three re-route rows are still in topo1's worklist after the restart.

**Also:** topo1's first three refill rows (t98A06, t98J01 and t98J02) all came back as "revise". That's ordinary review sending work back to the author, not a failure. You'll see those in `*topology-tail*` as "applied revise".
